### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b0c85a956b981d799c31bae9f38f46ed7cc0d06e` — the merge of head `94c3c852b947fe96f73ba6dcbde4e19ece968751` into base `a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b0c85a956b981d799c31bae9f38f46ed7cc0d06e && git checkout b0c85a956b981d799c31bae9f38f46ed7cc0d06e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b 94c3c852b947fe96f73ba6dcbde4e19ece968751 && git checkout -B drift-repro a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b && git merge --no-ff 94c3c852b947fe96f73ba6dcbde4e19ece968751

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f8644fa68538befef3b1c7dc382b933b891c4e39`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23096 (body; comments 6133319631 triage, 6133589472 claim, 6135259274 dev report); PR #23115 (body, 20-file list, net diff against `origin/main`, merge-base `36b2889cdd`, 561 added / 47 removed); the check-runs on the head; ADR-0010 on `origin/main`; and the rule texts the brief names (`pr-automation.yml` WHICH LEVEL, `clause2-line.mjs`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, ADR-0112, plus ADR-0016 §3.8 and ADR-0078 where they govern a quoted point). Read-only: git reads of the fetched ref and REST reads; nothing built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head, polled 2026-10-13T00:44Z: 31 success, 5 skipped (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance — all opt-in or path-gated), 4 still running: Test Core 3/6, 4/6, 5/6, 6/6. Green includes Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, Test Core 1/6 and 2/6, every Lint family, Type Check source / debt / consumer / workspace, Spec property liveness, Build Docs. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing below re-derives one.

### ① Derived judgments

**The branch — refusal is right against ADR-0010's actual text.** The ADR states one door for the block and states what a lock means for an environment item. Phase 4.3: "Public author surface (`packages/spec/src/shared/protection.zod.ts`) that translates into the private `_lock` envelope at load time" and "Loader (`metadata/plugin.ts` + `objectql/registry.ts`) calls `applyProtection(item, { packageId })` ... and strips the public `protection` block so it never leaks into the overlay row." §3.5: "`org` — Authored at runtime by a tenant via the metadata API. Set on first save." and "Tenant `org` artifacts ignore L3 / L4 entirely (the tenant owns them in full, can also delete them)." §3.2 puts a package's default lock in the manifest (`metadataDefaults`, unimplemented). §4.1 adds, of the protection fields: "The fields are stripped on write and reattached on load by the metadata loader." ADR-0016 §3.8 agrees for the Studio-authored package case: "Draft rows: editable/deletable (L3 `_lock` absent)" and "On publish, the sealed version's rows inherit the package `metadataDefaults.lock` (L2)". No ADR states a save-time `protection` door for an environment item, so triage's branch 3 (silent means refuse) is the one the text selects. §4.1's "stripped on write" does not argue for a silent strip of an author's block: a silent strip of a lock the author meant is the inert trap ADR-0078 forbids, and the strip is right only where the server rewrites its own rows (below). The dev read it right.

**The refusal — right on position, types, envelope and path.**
- Position in `saveMetaItem`: after the organization-scope refusal, the null-item guard, the name grammar and unmintable-type verdicts, the read-decoration / derived-provenance / system-column strips and the flow stamp rule, after L1 (code-only type), the package door (`refusePackagedBaseOverride`), the L3 `_lock` gate (`assertLockAllowsWrite`) and the object overlay mismatch; before the destructive diff, the per-type parse and the authoring gates. So a locked item still answers `403 ITEM_LOCKED` and a sealed one `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` (both pinned), and a malformed block meets this refusal rather than the parse's 422 (pinned). Nit, prose only: the code comment's "before every gate that reads or reshapes the body" overstates — three strips and the flow rule read the body earlier.
- Types: `overlaySchemaDeclaredKey(type, 'protection')` walks the registered schema through lazy, pipe, union, intersection and the optional family. On the head `packages/spec/src` carries 16 mounts of `protection: ProtectionSchema` (the 15 the dev lists plus the view flat-overlay arm at `view.zod.ts` line 5961, which carries no prose). A view item saved as `type: 'view'` with `viewKind` is refused through the union; nested `listViews` / `formViews` members declare no `protection`, so a nested block still meets the strict parse's 422. No declaring type escapes and no non-declaring type is touched (`page` control pinned).
- Envelope, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` beside the sibling's `422 INVALID_METADATA`: not a split the written rules forbid. ADR-0112 closes the vocabulary and derives status from code; both codes are ledger members of this package; `resolveThrownHttpError` (`packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts`) carries `issues` for any status, so `issues[0].path === 'protection'` reaches the REST wire, as the dev measured. The door already answers policy refusals of a parseable body in both envelopes (`savedItemNameRefusal` and the hook-without-body refusal at 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` at 422 `INVALID_METADATA`), so this adds no dialect the door does not already speak. Noted for the envelope-convergence line, not for this head: the closer fit by meaning is 422 — ADR-0010 §5.3 answers a path-level content refusal with 422 (`frozen_path`), and the sibling that refuses declared keys this door may not persist is 422 `INVALID_METADATA`. Moving it later is a second wire change; decide it once there.
- Located path: `protection` in the message and as the one `issues[]` entry (`code: 'custom'`), the `MetadataIssueEntry` shape. The message prescribes first, names ADR-0010's door, names no `_lock*` key (pinned), and stays under the 500-character REST bound for ordinary names.

**The strip — right, and the strip path is sealed from authors.** The split is `request.source !== undefined` or `writeFace === 'package-duplicate'`. Who states a `source`: `migrateStoredMetadata` (`protocol.ts`) and `flow-credential-migration.ts` (`@objectstack/service-automation`), both `'migrate-stored'`; who states the face: `duplicatePackage`. All three re-save rows the store already holds. The REST door builds its request field by field (`writeFace: 'meta-envelope'`) and never spreads the body; the dispatcher states `writeFace: 'meta-dispatch'` and no `source`; the unmanaged import states `'package-unmanaged-import'` and so takes the refusal path (pinned: a malformed block through that face is refused, a parseable one was already stripped by `stripUnmanagedImportLock`). No author-reachable write reaches the strip path. The caller's body is not mutated (pinned). Nit, pre-existing: the `protocol.ts` comment "the only caller that states a source" was already false before this PR (the credential move is a second caller).

**The narrowing (writable-base rows) — A is right.** ADR-0016 §3.8 locates a Studio-authored package's lock in `metadataDefaults` at publish, never in a per-item block at save; triage's invariant (no block persisted untranslated) forbids B; no producer in this repo writes the block through the door; the export use is unmeasured. A base author declares the lock in the manifest they install.

**The 15 TSDoc mounts, the module docblock and the reference page — true to the behaviour, no claim beyond it.** Every mount now says the loader translates and strips, and the metadata API's save door refuses with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` and stores nothing — exactly what the diff does. The old "strips this block before persistence" is gone from `packages/spec/src` and `content/docs` on the head (grepped). The view-item mount's sentence is true (saved as `view`, top-level key, union walk). `content/docs/references/shared/protection.mdx` regenerates from the module docblock paragraph verbatim. No `describe()` string moved, so no JSON schema or form surface changes.

**Tests and ledger.** Twelve cases run the real door over a row-keeping double with the producer's dispatch predicates; probes, draft, malformed, unmanaged face, open overlay, two rewrite strips, four controls; refusals asserted as `resolveThrownHttpError` envelopes. The pinned engine-double ledger gains the three rows the new file owes. Ablation both legs is dev-reported and consistent with the diff.

PR-body nit: "`applyProtection` is reused through `overlaySchemaDeclaredKey`" is not what the code does — `overlaySchemaDeclaredKey` reads the schema and the new code never calls `applyProtection`, which is the point (no translation is copied). Prose only.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor` — right. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the arm `clause2-line.mjs` defines for "NOT a widening, but breaking". Under WHICH LEVEL, `major` stays refused in the launch window and breaking-ness rides the BREAKING banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not the level; a `fix(` that changes a public surface — here the door's accept set — is not the "changes no public surface stays `patch`" case, so `minor` is the floor the act sets. The level axis stands down on a `no` declaration; banner and disposition are both present.

`@objectstack/spec: patch` — right: TSDoc prose only, no `describe()`, no type, no value domain.

`not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — right for this narrowing, on three grounds. (i) The gate refuses the category only where the changeset prescribes a rewrite of a consumer's code or metadata; here the remedy is a request value at one runtime door, the argument five stock entries already carry in the same `FROM / TO / Remedy` shape (`15196-position-environment-write-through`, `15196-s10-position-namespace`, `15196-s5a-resolver-grant-name`, `15205-email-template-org-door-closed`, `15206-managed-content-sealed`). (ii) A ledger entry would be wrong, not merely unneeded: an ADR-0087 conversion replays over package sources and at every rehydration seam alike (`migrations/types.ts` scopes an entry by `surface`, never by store), so a conversion that strips `protection` would strip a package source's legitimate declaration — the one place ADR-0010 says it belongs. (iii) What the disposition leaves behind, stated so no one reads more into the changeset than it says: a row stored before this change keeps its inert block, and `migrateStoredMetadata` records such a row `canonical` and never rewrites it (it re-saves only rows a conversion changed — `if (!changed) ... continue`), so the strip path clears it only when some other conversion fires on that row. The changeset's sentence is conditional and true, and its Remedy covers the Studio round-trip (the served body carries the block, the 400 names it, the author deletes it). No ledger entry follows; see flag 1 for the one sentence the changeset does owe.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **BLOCKING — a same-release contract contradiction this PR's changeset must supersede.** `.changeset/15213-unmanaged-lock-strip.md` sits in `origin/main`'s unreleased stock (bumps `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/cli`) and states: "a malformed `protection` block ... is not stripped: the save door refuses that item as before, `422 INVALID_METADATA`, and the install is rolled back." At this head that case on a declaring type answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` — this PR pins exactly it ("on the unmanaged import's face ... `lock: 'sealed'`"), and `rollBackUnmanagedImport` relays the cause's code and status to the install-local door and the CLI. Both bodies ship verbatim as `CHANGELOG.md` in one release, so the release contradicts itself on one refusal. The house form is in that sibling itself: "This entry supersedes two sentences of the entry `15213-install-modes`, in this same release." Fix, one sentence in `.changeset/23096-save-door-protection.md`: name `15213-unmanaged-lock-strip` and state that its `protection` limb now meets this `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` while its `_lock` limbs keep the parse's `422` (an unknown `_lock` value still fails the enum at the parse; verified on the head's gate order). Rider in the same push, not a condition: `stripUnmanagedImportLock`'s docblock "refuses it as before" in `package-unmanaged-install.ts` gains the same clause — the dev noted the drift with no carrier, and the file is this family's, in this PR's package.
2. **Raw `_lock` at the save door — a follow-up card, not this PR's.** The dev measured on a showcase boot: `PUT` with `_lock: 'full'` answers 200, the lock binds (403 `ITEM_LOCKED` on the next `PUT` and on `DELETE`), and no unlock door exists (ADR-0010 §3.8 is unimplemented). Contract: ADR-0010 §3.5 (org items ignore L3), §4.1 ("stripped on write"), `shared/protection.zod.ts` ("never authored"). But `item-lock.ts` carries the triage ruling on #21738 reading a stored row's lock as an administrator's lock (`ITEM_LOCK_LAYERS` names `overlay` as a layer), so closing it reverses a recorded direction and needs its own card and ruling; this PR's scope is the public block, and triage gave one branch. The dev did not file it (Prime Directive 10 says a measured contract violation is filed). Seat action: file it with the dev's dedupe words.
3. **`flow-clone.ts` omission — a follow-up card for the runtime lane, non-blocking.** `FLOW_CLONE_DROPPED_KEYS` drops `MetadataProtectionFields` and the read decorations but not `protection`; `PERMISSION_SET_CLONE_DROPPED_KEYS` lists it. Confirmed path: `cloneFlowDefinition` into `registerAndSaveFlow` into `saveMetaItem` with no `source` and no face, so a clone of a flow whose stored body carries a pre-change block is refused with a message the clone caller cannot act on from the clone dialog. Same class, same PR effect: `packages.ts`'s `_unpublished` re-flag re-saves a served `app` body with no source. Population: rows stored before this change only (loader-hydrated items are stripped by `applyProtection`; no producer writes the block through the door). Loud, with a remedy an admin can perform on the source row, so it does not block; the card decides whether the clone doors drop `protection` or server-composed re-saves state a face that strips.
4. Dev deviations, each answered: the `(narrowing)` arm — right (②); strip instead of refuse on server-stated rewrites — right (①); the two gate-prescribed files — right; one merge of `origin/main` — fine; the envelope — right for this head, with the convergence note (①); the verify-lock duration and the one blocked shell command — process, no effect on the diff.
5. Open question A or B — A (①).
6. Out-of-scope prose: the stale `protocol.ts` "only caller that states a source" comment — pre-existing, for the owning seat's next pass.
7. Four Test Core shards were still running at the poll above; the landing waits on them whatever this verdict says.

Adopted by `domain:engine` seat 2 at 2026-10-13T00:45Z, after a tool-use audit of the isolated reviewer's transcript: reads, `git fetch` into a review ref, and writes to its own record only. It made no GitHub write and ran no build, test or gate. The seat re-read the blocking finding: `.changeset/15213-unmanaged-lock-strip.md` on `main` (line 17) states a malformed `protection` block is refused `422 INVALID_METADATA`, and this head answers 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` on declaring types, with no supersession in this PR's changeset.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `94c3c852b947fe96f73ba6dcbde4e19ece968751`
Local-runs: none

Delta review after the FAIL record 6135514431 on `f8644fa685`. Inputs: card #23096 (body; comments 6133319631 triage, 6133589472 claim, 6135259274 and 6136167340 dev reports, 6135569879 seat note); PR #23115 (the seat-edited body, the 21-file list, the net diff against `main` from merge-base `36b2889cdd`, 570 added / 49 removed, the delta `f8644fa685..94c3c852b9`, and its comments including the prior record); the check-runs on the head; `.changeset/15213-unmanaged-lock-strip.md` on `origin/main`; and, where a quoted point needed its source, `protocol.ts`, `package-unmanaged-install.ts`, the two test files and the three non-declaring spec schemas at the head, read with `git show` on the fetched ref. Read-only: git reads of the review ref and REST reads; nothing built, run or re-run. The escalation issues #23119 and #23120 were read for their state only.

Check-runs on the head, polled 2026-10-13T01:45Z: 48, all completed, 41 success, 7 skipped, 0 failed, 0 running. The skipped ones are opt-in or path-gated (Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shard, Packed-tarball smoke) plus Check PR Size and Auto Label on the second pr-automation run that the body edit triggered. Green includes Check Changeset (twice, on both runs), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core and all six shards, every Lint family, Type Check source / debt / consumer / workspace, and Spec property liveness. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing below re-derives one.

### ① Derived judgments

**The delta is prose only.** `git diff f8644fa685 94c3c852b9`: two files, 9 added / 2 removed. `.changeset/23096-save-door-protection.md` gains one paragraph (the supersession) and its blank line. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts` changes seven lines, every one inside the `stripUnmanagedImportLock` docblock (each line is `*`-prefixed comment text; no statement, token or export moves). The net diff against `main` at this head is the prior 20 files plus that one, with the same merge-base; `protocol.ts`, the new test, the 16 spec mounts, the reference page and the pinned ledger are byte-identical to `f8644fa685`. No governed path. So there is no code to re-review; the paragraph and the docblock are judged against the code the prior record already read.

**The supersession paragraph is true against the code at this head, on all three claims.**

- (a) A malformed block, or a block beside a refused `_lock*` value, on a declaring type, through the unmanaged install: 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, rolled back. `stripUnmanagedImportLock` returns the body UNTOUCHED when any envelope key fails its declaration (the `envelopeKeys.every(...)` guard) or when the block fails `protectionDeclaration.safeParse`, so in both cases the block rides to the door. `importUnmanagedPackage` saves each item with `writeFace: 'package-unmanaged-import'` and no `source`, which is the refusal arm of the split in `saveMetaItem` (`request.source === undefined && request.writeFace !== 'package-duplicate'`). That arm runs after `assertLockAllowsWrite` and before the per-type parse that mints the 422; the only earlier body-reading refusal, `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal`, answers `null` for every type but `flow` and for a flow judges provenance stamps and the named base, never `_lock*`. `protectionBlockRefusal` fires on any own, defined `protection` value on a type `overlaySchemaDeclaredKey` says declares it. `rollBackUnmanagedImport` uninstalls the target base and returns an error carrying the cause's `code`, `status` and `issues` with `details.rolledBack`, so the install-local door and the CLI see 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`. The malformed limb is pinned on the import's face in `protocol.save-door-protection.test.ts` (`lock: 'sealed'`); the beside-a-refused-`_lock` limb is the same path by construction and is dev-measured through a non-committed probe, not pinned.
- (b) A refused `_lock*` value with no block: 422 `INVALID_METADATA`. `DERIVED_PROVENANCE_KEYS` is `_packageId`, `_packageVersion`, `_provenance` and its header excludes the `_lock*` family on purpose; `stripServedObjectColumns` is object-scoped; with no block `protectionBlockRefusal` returns `undefined`; the parse then judges `_lock` by `MetadataLockSchema` (`none`, `no-overlay`, `no-delete`, `full`) and `_lockReason` by `z.string().max(500)`, both spread on the type schemas through `MetadataProtectionFields`, and mints 422 `INVALID_METADATA`. Pinned through the import in `package-unmanaged-install.test.ts` (`apps: [{ ..., _lock: 'locked' }]`, 422, rolled back), green on this head.
- (c) A block on a type that declares none (`action`, `hook`, `page`): 422 `INVALID_METADATA`. None of the three mounts `protection` (each spreads only `MetadataProtectionFields`), so `overlaySchemaDeclaredKey` answers `undefined`, the refusal is not asked, and the parse judges; `actionObject()`, `HookSchema` and `PageSchema` are all `strictObject` at the head, so the block is an unrecognized key. Pinned for `page` both at the door (the new test's control) and through the import (the sibling test, rolled back). This PR does not touch the limb.

The three claims partition the sibling sentence's cases completely: a malformed block on a non-declaring type falls under (c), and a valid block beside a valid `_lock` is stripped and saved, which the sentence never covered.

**It names the sibling the way the house form requires.** The form is the one the three precedent entries on `main` use (`15213-install-modes`, `15213-unmanaged-lock-strip`, `22521-config-boot-residual`): a bold lead sentence naming the superseded entry by its file stem in a code span with "in this same release", "That entry says" with a verbatim quotation, "What holds now:", and the closing "Where the two entries disagree, this one is current." The new paragraph has every limb; the quotation "the save door refuses that item as before, `422 INVALID_METADATA`, and the install is rolled back" matches the sibling's line verbatim. No script reads the form (none in `scripts/` or the workflows names it); the sibling file is untouched, as the house form requires. One residual, prose only: the sibling's closing sentence "every refusal of the unmanaged install is unchanged" now also disagrees in one envelope, and the paragraph's closing clause already settles which entry is current.

**The docblock is true.** Each statement checks against the function it heads and the door it names: the untouched hand-on for a refused envelope value or a malformed block (the two early returns), the 422 for a refused `_lock*` value (the parse, with the keys surviving to it as shown under (b)), the 400 FIRST for a block on a declaring type (the gate order under (a)), the function name `protectionBlockRefusal` in `protocol.ts` (it exists, module-level, called once), and the pre-existing "left in place" bullet for a non-declaring type (strict parse, (c)).

**The prior record's ① judgments hold on this head.** They were rendered on code this delta does not touch: the refusal branch against ADR-0010, the position of `protectionBlockRefusal` in `saveMetaItem`, the 16 declaring mounts, the envelope and the located path, the strip path sealed from authors, option A on writable-base rows, the 15 TSDoc mounts and the reference page, and the twelve test cases with the ledger rows. Nothing in the net diff against `main` outside the delta differs from what that record read. The PR-body nit it named ("`applyProtection` is reused through `overlaySchemaDeclaredKey`") is corrected in the seat-edited body, which now says the new code never calls `applyProtection`; the body's "before every gate that reads or reshapes the body" is corrected too, while the same overstatement remains in the `protocol.ts` call-site comment (dev declined under "no other change"; prose, see ③).
